newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese park's snake stunt denounced.
newsitem.headline: Chinese park's snake stunt denounced.

text.p: Hong Kong human rights activists have denounced an amusement park in southern China where six members of a "snake clan" -- including two children -- were locked in a glass cage with thousands of poisonous snakes in an attempt to break a record that does not exist.
The Sunday Morning Post reported from the southern Chinese city of Panyu that the six had been bitten repeatedly during their time in the cage.
About one-third of the 38,888 snakes, which included cobras and rattlesnakes, were poisonous, it said.

A spokesman from the Flying Dragon World Park told the newspaper the "snake people" were from a clan whose ancestors had a history of involvement with snakes and had agreed to live with the reptiles in a 200 square metre (yard) glass-walled enclosure for 100 days, which ended on Sunday.
The newspaper also quoted a spokeswoman for the London-based Guinness Book of World Records as saying the stunt would not be accepted as a record.
"We have taken out the marathon category from our records because some people had been eating, drinking and sleeping during the process, which makes it meaningless," Carol Jones told the Post.

The newpaper quoted the three-year-old Lei Hongmei as saying she was bitten several times. The last bite, a week ago, had left a deep scar on her finger. "I cried and I wanted to go out," she told the Post.
Hong Kong Human Rights Commission chairman Ho Hei-wah urged tourists to boycott the park.
The Flying Dragon World opened two years ago and is famed for its thousands of snakes. It attracts three million visitors a year, about 750,000 of them from Hong Kong.
